findings.title: Team admin check uses && and so needs the user to be OWNER; admins are refused
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-270). `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER (:286-293). Joining them with `&&` makes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` true only for owners, so a team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins are allowed. Use `isTeamAdmin(...)` alone, or join the two with `||`.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses its `newGuests` argument to decide who gets the new-booking `AttendeeScheduledEmail` and who gets the "guests added" email (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:540-546). The handler passes the raw `guests` input, not the filtered `uniqueGuests` (line 74). If the input includes someone who is already an attendee, the handler filters them out and does not add them again, but they still get a fresh "new event scheduled" email instead of the update email. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Server never de-duplicates the list or compares case-insensitively, so duplicate attendees get created and the blacklist can be bypassed
findings.body: The server schema is just `z.array(z.string().email())` (addGuests.schema.ts:5). The uniqueness refine exists only in the dialog (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29), so an API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` makes two attendee rows through `createMany` (lines 92-106). The filter also compares exact strings. `guest === attendee.email` lets `A@x.com` be added next to an existing `a@x.com`. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (line 71) but `guest` is not, so `Spam@blocked.com` gets past a `spam@blocked.com` entry. Lowercase the guests and de-duplicate them before filtering.

findings.title: Any attendee can make the app email an unlimited list of arbitrary addresses
findings.body: Matching on email alone lets any logged-in user whose email is on a booking (for example someone who booked a public event) add guests, and the guests array has no upper bound (addGuests.schema.ts:5). Every call sends the organizer, team members and every attendee an email from the app's mailer (email-manager.ts:525-549). That is a spam and amplification path. Consider capping `guests` with `.max(...)` and deciding whether attendees should have this permission at all.

findings.title: A stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error stays after a successful add or after closing the dialog
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` runs only in the Cancel handler (line 91). If a submit fails validation, the user corrects it and the add succeeds, `onSuccess` clears the emails but not `isInvalidEmail`, so the next time the dialog opens it shows the error at once. Closing with Esc or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61) also keeps the old emails and the old error. Reset both on success and whenever the dialog closes.

findings.title: Error toast fallback can never run, and it can show 'undefined: …'
findings.body: `message` is a template string and is never empty, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data` is missing (for example a network error), the toast reads `undefined: <raw message>`. Build the code prefix only when `err.data?.code` exists, and fall back to `unable_to_add_guests` when there is no message.
